novel_mechanics_found: Level 3 changes the familiar horizontal reorder into a pinned vertical stack. The patterned reel can thread a horizontal tether through a colored segment; a vertical move then carries every intersected segment into the next free row, while fully retracting the tether detaches the carried group so another row can be selected. The small color-B glyph above the stack appears to anchor or stop upward movement. ACTION5 and coordinate-click ACTION6 were tested on the glyph, blocks, guide, and reel and were frame-level no-ops.
narrative: The generic resolver returned only the stale 14-action L1 artifact, so I followed the registry's named results/arc_loop_solve_sk48.json fallback and confirmed its 44-action sequence reaches level 2. On level 3 I explored all direction verbs, ACTION5, and clicks using only rendered frame deltas. I learned how to separate the bottom C segment, detach it by fully retracting the reel, and build a stable partial 8,C arrangement while separating 9, but did not observe a level-3 win. I stopped before the 600-step cap so the highest complete 44-action sequence could be replayed through the mandatory fresh-reset gate; that gate reproduced level 2 successfully.
gotchas: resolve_replay_plan returned the older 14-action L1 source even for levels_reproduced=2; the registry-named results/arc_loop_solve_sk48.json contains the working 44-action L2 prefix.
ACTION1/ACTION2 move the reel vertically and ACTION3/ACTION4 retract/extend it horizontally, but a colored segment moves vertically only when the tether intersects its row.
A partial retraction may only erase surplus tether pixels; fully retract before moving the reel independently to select another segment row.
Trying to lift an intersected segment into an occupied/pinned row is a no-op; separate lower segments into free rows before recombining them.
ACTION5 and ACTION6 clicks produced no rendered change on level 3 in the tested locations.
